content:
Looking at the folds: the octagon is folded along a vertical axis, then a horizontal axis, then a diagonal axis, producing a triangle whose vertices are the center of the octagon and two adjacent octagon vertices. The cut is made perpendicular to one of the fold lines (the horizontal cut in the diagram), slicing off the corner at the center of the octagon.

When unfolded, the cut segment is reflected across the three fold lines (vertical, horizontal, diagonal), producing 8 copies. Because the cut line is perpendicular to one fold axis and meets the diagonal fold axis at √2 times the distance from the center, the 8 reflected segments join up to form four straight lines — the sides of a square aligned with the fold axes (horizontal and vertical sides), centered in the octagon.

Checking the options: a regular octagonal hole would require the cut to be equidistant on both fold edges (it isn't); a star would require a slanted cut crossing one edge much closer to the center; tilted squares and rotated octagons cannot arise from these symmetry lines. The result is an axis-aligned square hole.

\boxed{C}
